subject: SwiftPath pilot: parallel request needs & quota calibration
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Lee Chen <lee@swiftpath.com>, Anna Morales <anna@swiftpath.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: SwiftPath pilot: parallel request needs & quota calibration

Hi Lee / Anna —

Thanks again for the call today — helpful to see the latency targets and the streaming use cases. As promised, summary and concrete asks so we can lock the pilot configuration and rate limits: 

What we heard from your side (please confirm):
- P95 latency target: <= 150ms for synchronous generation (short prompts, avg. 120 tokens).
- Streaming sessions: ~30% of requests will use WebSocket streaming (server push) with partials every ~200ms.
- Concurrency: expected steady-state parallel request concurrency ~200 simultaneous requests across 6 backend instances. Peak bursts could reach ~400 concurrent requests for 1–2 minute windows.
- Throughput: baseline 150 QPS sustained, with 3–4x spiky bursts during batch runs.
- Token size assumptions: avg. 120 tokens in, 80 tokens out per request.
- Data retention: ephemeral KV cache per-session, no long-term storage.

Redwood pilot proposal / initial constraints: 
- Baseline quota: 200 concurrent sessions (websocket or HTTP), 150 QPS sustained.
- Burst window: token-based burst pool equivalent to +50% concurrency for 2-minute windows (configurable).
- Rate-limit behavior: 429 with Retry-After header for rate exceed; automatic fallback to a compatible smaller model if a session is throttled (optional).
- Observability: per-route latency and connection occupancy in Console; we'll grant the SwiftPath team dashboard access for the pilot.

Attachments: I attached the PoC requirements spreadsheet and a short terms summary for the pilot package.

Asks / next steps (please reply inline):
1) Confirm the concurrency and burst assumptions above. If you expect long-tail requests (>>300 tokens), call that out — it affects KV cache footprint and concurrency economics.
2) Is WebSocket streaming mandatory for all streaming flows or can we switch to chunked HTTP for some flows?
3) Procurement: who should I loop in from your side to start an SOW? I added procure@swiftpath.com as a guess.
4) Can you share an example request pattern (CSV or simple histogram) for an hour of peak traffic? That will help us refine batching and pre-warm recommendations.

If this matches your expectations, we can move to a pilot SOW with a 30-day trial: 200 baseline concurrent sessions, +100 burst tokens, and a limited throughput SLA for the pilot window.

Thanks —
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Attachment(s): swiftpath_poc_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_pilot_package_terms.pdf (pdf)

From: Lee Chen <lee@swiftpath.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Morales <anna@swiftpath.com>, procure@swiftpath.com
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SwiftPath pilot: parallel request needs & quota calibration

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the concise recap — this lines up with what we discussed with a couple clarifications:

- The 150ms p95 is for the customer-facing endpoint where we do short-turn summarization. For internal analytics jobs we'll tolerate higher latency (up to 500ms).
- Streaming: WebSocket is preferred for the UI flows (live typing), but we can use chunked HTTP for scheduled batch exports. Expect ~40% of front-end requests to be WebSocket streaming during heavy hours.
- Concurrency: the 200 steady-state is per-region (we have users mostly in US-East). We may spin up a second region in Q4.
- Bursts: the 400 concurrent spike is realistic for demo days. Peaks last ~3–5 minutes rather than 1–2.

Procurement: procure@swiftpath.com is our contracts mailbox. Please loop in Anna Morales (CTO) for technical acceptance.

I attached a short CSV with a 1-hour sample of peak traffic (columns: timestamp, active_sessions, avg_in_tokens, avg_out_tokens).

We'll review the pilot terms and get back with a preferred start date — aiming to start the week of Oct 6.

Appreciate the clear next steps.

—Lee
Principal Product Manager | SwiftPath Health
lee@swiftpath.com

Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SwiftPath pilot: parallel request needs & quota calibration

Olga / Marissa —

Quick internal note before we lock terms with procurement:
- Commercial stance: offer a pilot package (30 days free) with the following negotiated defaults: 200 baseline concurrent sessions, 100 concurrent burst tokens (effective peak 300), and 150 QPS sustained. Provide 2x credits if SwiftPath exceeds pilot ceilings while we're triaging.
- If they want guaranteed 400 peak, propose a small monthly reserved commit for Dedicated: start at 250 reserved sessions + 30% burst for an annual price — we can model the unit economics later.
- Ask for permission to enable our automated prefix caching for high-frequency prompts (should reduce token costs significantly).

Operational asks for the SOW: include explicit websocket concurrency semantics (idle timeout, KV cache excluded from concurrency), and a plan for graceful 429 behavior + suggested client retry backoff.

I'll draft the commercial note and SOW language.

Ben
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Lee Chen <lee@swiftpath.com>, procure@swiftpath.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SwiftPath pilot: parallel request needs & quota calibration

Lee / Procurement team —

Thanks — all good notes. Based on your sample CSV and Ben's commercial framing, here's a concise pilot SOW offer we can accept immediately if you confirm: 

Pilot offer (30 days):
- Baseline concurrent sessions: 200 (region: us-east).
- Burst pool: 100 concurrent tokens available per 2-minute window (effective short-term peak 300).
- Sustained throughput: 150 QPS.
- Streaming: WebSocket supported for UI flows; chunked HTTP for batch flows. Idle timeout for websocket sessions: 120s.
- Behavior on exceed: 429 + Retry-After; we will also expose a per-route congestion metric in Console.
- Observability: dashboard access + one onboarding session with Solutions (60m).
- Credits: If an unexpected quota block hits during the pilot, we'll issue an operational credit and keep sessions active while we triage (limited to two incidents).

Next steps: 
1) Procurement — please confirm the procurement contact and whether you need a DocuSign SOW or a PO first.
2) Tech — Lee / Anna: confirm that the 3–5 minute burst window is the correct expectation. If so, we'll provision the burst pool to handle that profile.
3) Dates — propose start week of Oct 6; production traffic ramp plan due 3 business days after SOW signature.

If that works, I'll push the SOW draft and the pilot config into HubSpot and share the DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com
